speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder. To help me understand what is happening, have you noticed any tremors, stiffness, or changes in your gait recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very helpful information; the timing of your movement disorder symptoms starting two months after initiating risperidone is significant. To better understand the nature of this issue, are these movements involuntary, such as rhythmic shaking or repetitive movements you cannot control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—feeling unable to sit still, fidgeting, and pacing—are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent initiation of risperidone, this is a likely side effect. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness or tremors as well? REQUEST TEST: Physical_Examination_Neurological.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mental_Status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Improved psychotic symptoms. Cranial_Nerves: Intact. Motor: Normal tone and strength in all extremities. No involuntary movements noted. Sensory: Intact. Coordination: Normal. Gait: Normal, but patient exhibits inability to sit still with frequent pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia secondary to risperidone. The clinical picture of severe inner restlessness, fidgeting, and pacing, combined with the absence of rigidity or tremors on neurological exam, strongly confirms this side effect. We can proceed with management to alleviate these distressing symptoms.
